verdict.headline: This policy sharply limits cover for chronic conditions: it pays only up to 12 months from the first paid benefit, then stops and pushes ongoing care to the NHS.
verdict.summary: The key issue in this text is not the price of the policy but a major limit on what treatment you can actually use it for. The policy defines chronic conditions broadly, including conditions that continue indefinitely, need long-term monitoring, or are likely to come back, then says benefits stop after 12 months from the first paid claim for that condition. That means treatment, monitoring, and maintenance medication for many longer-lasting illnesses may become your responsibility or move to NHS care much sooner than a reader might expect from private health insurance.

topFindings.title: Cover for chronic conditions ends 12 months after the first paid claim
topFindings.shortWhy: The policy says it will pay for eligible treatment of a chronic condition for only 12 months from the date it first pays a benefit, and after that 'no further benefits will be payable' for that condition.

topFindings.title: The policy's definition of 'chronic condition' is broad and can capture recurring or long-managed illnesses
topFindings.shortWhy: A condition counts as chronic if it needs long-term monitoring, symptom control, rehabilitation, continues indefinitely, has no known cure, or 'comes back or is likely to come back'.

topFindings.title: Monitoring and maintenance medication are specifically excluded after the 12-month limit
topFindings.shortWhy: The text expressly excludes 'ongoing monitoring, maintenance medication, and management of chronic conditions beyond the 12-month period'.

topClauseLabels: No cover for monitoring or maintenance after the cutoff
